question: For normal distribution, which of the following is true?
solution:
The correct answer is **Mean = Median = Mode**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• **The property that the mean, median, and mode are equal in a normal distribution is a fundamental characteristic of its symmetrical shape.**

 
 
• In a normal distribution, the data is symmetrically distributed around the mean, creating a bell-shaped curve. The mean represents the arithmetic average of the data points, indicating the central tendency of the distribution.
 
• The median, on the other hand, represents the middle value that divides the distribution into two equal halves. The mode refers to the value that occurs most frequently in the dataset.
 
• Since the normal distribution is symmetric, with equal proportions of data on both sides of the mean, the median and mode coincide with the mean. This means that the central value of the distribution, which represents the peak or highest point, is also the value that occurs most frequently and divides the data into equal halves.
 
• The equality of the mean, median, and mode in a normal distribution simplifies the understanding and analysis of the data. It provides a reference point for locating the center of the distribution and understanding the typical value that represents the dataset.
 
• This property also facilitates various statistical calculations and inference procedures based on the normal distribution, as it allows for simpler computations and interpretations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6dc61ece8bc24f80b29971eeae9304c77127cdd7d6d17c41a66feda07785c8af.png] 

 
• **Hence, the fact that the mean, median, and mode are equal in a normal distribution is true.**
